questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Why should a base class destructor almost always be declared `virtual` if the class has virtual functions?

options.A: To allow private member destruction
options.B: To ensure derived class destructors are called when deleting via base pointer

questions.explanation: Deleting a derived object through a base class pointer without a virtual destructor causes undefined behavior (derived destructor skipped).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: How does C++ solve the 'Diamond Problem' (duplicate base subobjects) in multiple inheritance?

options.A: By using virtual base classes (`class Derived : public virtual Base`)

questions.explanation: Virtual base classes ensure that only one shared subobject instance of the base class exists in the inheritance hierarchy.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the signature of a move constructor for class `Widget` in C++11?

options.A: Widget(const Widget& other);

questions.explanation: Move constructors take an rvalue reference `Widget&&` and should be marked `noexcept` for STL optimization.

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: Rule of Three, Rule of Five, and Rule of Zero
questions.question: According to the Rule of Five in modern C++, if a class defines a custom destructor, what four other special member functions should it also explicitly define or default/delete?

options.A: Copy constructor, copy assignment, move constructor, move assignment
options.B: Default constructor, parameterized constructor, static constructor, friend function
options.C: Virtual function, pure virtual function, override, final

questions.explanation: The Rule of Five covers Destructor, Copy Constructor, Copy Assignment, Move Constructor, and Move Assignment.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens when `std::make_shared<T>()` is used instead of `std::shared_ptr<T>(new T())`?

options.A: Allocates object and control block in a single contiguous memory block
options.B: Runs slower but uses less memory
options.D: Allows multiple pointers without reference counting

questions.explanation: std::make_shared performs a single memory allocation for both object and control block, improving cache locality and efficiency.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is SFINAE in C++ template metaprogramming?

options.A: Substitution Failure Is An Error
options.B: Substitution Failure Is Not An Error

questions.explanation: SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) ignores invalid template argument substitutions during overload resolution rather than failing compilation.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which operation on `std::vector<int>` invalidates ALL existing iterators and references to its elements?

options.A: push_back() when current capacity is exceeded (triggering reallocation)

questions.explanation: When vector capacity is exceeded, reallocation moves all elements to new memory, invalidating all outstanding iterators.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens if a lambda captures a local automatic variable by reference `[&x]`, and outlives the lifetime of `x`?

options.A: The variable is kept alive automatically on heap
options.B: Invoking the lambda results in undefined behavior (dangling reference)

questions.explanation: Capturing local variables by reference when the lambda outlives their scope produces dangling references and undefined behavior.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: In C++11 template deduction, what does `T&&` collapse to when instantiated with an lvalue of type `X&`? (Reference Collapsing Rules)
questions.explanation: Reference collapsing rules state: & + & -> &, & + && -> &, && + & -> &, && + && -> &&. So X& + && collapses to X&.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the status of reading an uninitialized local variable of primitive type `int x;` in C++?

options.A: Guaranteed to be 0

questions.explanation: Reading uninitialized automatic scalar variables yields indeterminate values, causing undefined behavior.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: How do you distinguish between pre-increment `++obj` and post-increment `obj++` when overloading member operators in C++?

options.A: Post-increment accepts a dummy int parameter: `Type operator++(int);`

questions.explanation: The dummy parameter `int` in `operator++(int)` distinguishes post-increment from pre-increment `operator++()`.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What does the Strong Exception Safety Guarantee mandate for a function in C++?

options.A: The function never throws exceptions
options.B: If the function throws an exception, program state is rolled back to exactly before the call (commit-or-rollback semantics)
options.C: No memory leaks occur but state may change

questions.explanation: The strong exception guarantee ensures that if an exception occurs, object and program state remains completely unchanged.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Why should move constructors and move assignment operators be marked `noexcept`?

options.A: To allow standard containers like std::vector to safely use move operations during reallocation
options.B: To make them run on GPU

questions.explanation: std::vector reallocation uses std::move_if_noexcept; without noexcept, vector falls back to copying for strong exception safety.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is non-virtual interface (NVI) idiom in C++ software design?

options.A: Declaring all functions virtual
options.B: Making public base functions non-virtual while delegating to private/protected virtual implementations
options.C: Using templates instead of virtual functions

questions.explanation: NVI idiom exposes public non-virtual interface methods that enforce invariant checks before calling private/protected virtual implementation methods.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens when two `std::shared_ptr` objects are created independently from the same raw pointer `int* raw = new int(10);`?

options.A: They share the reference counter correctly
options.B: They create two separate control blocks, resulting in double deletion (undefined behavior)

questions.explanation: Creating multiple shared_ptrs from a raw pointer independently creates multiple control blocks leading to double free corruption upon destruction.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is Perfect Forwarding in C++11 and what standard function implements it?

options.A: Preserving value categories (lvalue/rvalue) of arguments when passing them using `std::forward<T>()` and forwarding references (`T&&`)

questions.explanation: Perfect forwarding uses universal/forwarding references (`T&&`) and `std::forward<T>()` to preserve parameter lvalueness/rvalueness.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is memory alignment and structure padding in C++ classes?

options.A: Inserting unused padding bytes between data members to align variables to architecture memory boundaries

questions.explanation: Compilers insert padding bytes between fields to align multi-byte types to CPU word boundaries for efficient bus access.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the average and worst-case time complexity of lookup in `std::unordered_map`?

options.A: Average O(1), Worst-case O(N)
options.B: Average O(log N), Worst-case O(log N)

questions.explanation: std::unordered_map has average O(1) time complexity, but degrades to O(N) worst-case when high hash collisions occur.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What does the `[[nodiscard]]` attribute in C++17 warn the developer about?

options.A: Function parameter cannot be null
options.B: The return value of the function should not be discarded/ignored by caller

questions.explanation: [[nodiscard]] issues a compiler warning if a function caller discards its return value.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is strict aliasing rule violation in C++?

options.A: Accessing an object through a pointer of an incompatible type that does not share its effective type (except char/unsigned char)
options.C: Assigning base pointer to derived pointer

questions.explanation: Strict aliasing allows compiler optimizations assuming incompatible type pointers don't alias; violating it yields undefined behavior.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is fold expression introduced in C++17?

options.A: Compressing array elements into string
options.B: Syntax for reducing variadic template parameter packs over binary operators

questions.explanation: C++17 fold expressions simplify reductions over variadic template parameter packs (e.g., `(... + args)`).

questions.explanation: Assigning derived object 'b' to base object 'a' causes Object Slicing. 'a' is a pure A object, calling A::show().

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is decltype in C++11?

options.A: Yields the declared type of an expression/variable at compile time

questions.explanation: decltype inspects and yields the precise declared type of an entity or expression at compile time.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Why does `std::make_unique` not allow custom deleters directly compared to `std::unique_ptr` constructor?

options.A: Custom deleters change the type signature of std::unique_ptr<T, Deleter>
options.D: It is a bug in C++14

questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr type parameter incorporates the Deleter type `unique_ptr<T, Deleter>`; custom deleters alter class type.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is copy elision and Return Value Optimization (RVO)?

options.A: Compiler optimization technique that eliminates unnecessary copying/moving of objects during return by constructing directly in caller target

questions.explanation: RVO constructs return objects directly inside the caller's memory space, eliding copy/move constructor calls.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which member operator overload MUST return a reference to `*this` to support chained assignments `a = b = c;`?

options.A: Copy assignment operator `Class& operator=(const Class& rhs)`

questions.explanation: Returning `Class&` by reference allows chaining assignment calls `a = (b = c);`.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens if an abstract class declares a pure virtual destructor `virtual ~Base() = 0;`?

options.A: The base class destructor must still be provided with a body definition outside class

questions.explanation: Base class destructors are always called during derived destruction, so a pure virtual destructor MUST have a definition body.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the time complexity of `std::vector::insert` at an arbitrary iterator position in the middle of a vector?

options.B: O(N) due to shifting subsequent elements

questions.explanation: Inserting in the middle of a vector requires shifting all following elements to the right, taking linear time O(N).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is structured binding introduced in C++17?

options.A: Syntax to unpack tuples, pairs, or structs into individual named variables `auto [x, y] = point;`

questions.explanation: Structured bindings allow decomposing tuple-like types or structs into discrete local identifiers.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What does `std::optional<T>` in C++17 represent?

options.A: A container that manages a value that may or may not be present

questions.explanation: std::optional<T> represents a value wrapper that explicitly conveys presence or absence of a value without heap allocation.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the average time complexity of `std::sort` in C++ standard library implementations (Introsort)?

options.A: O(N log N) worst-case and average guaranteed

questions.explanation: Introsort hybrid (Quick sort + Heap sort fallback + Insertion sort) guarantees O(N log N) worst-case time.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is `std::variant<Types...>` introduced in C++17?

options.A: A type-safe, discriminative union container holding one value from a set of alternative types

questions.explanation: std::variant is a type-safe union that tracks its active type index.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which standard header file provides multi-threading primitives like `std::thread` in C++11?

options.A: <thread>

questions.explanation: <thread> declares std::thread class for managing concurrent execution threads.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens if a `std::thread` object is destroyed while still joinable (without calling `join()` or `detach()`)?

options.A: std::terminate() is called immediately

questions.explanation: Destroying a joinable thread object calls std::terminate(), ending program execution.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which RAII wrapper class automatically locks a `std::mutex` on construction and unlocks it on destruction?

options.A: std::lock_guard

questions.explanation: std::lock_guard provides RAII-style scope locking for std::mutex.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is `std::string_view` introduced in C++17?

options.A: A non-owning read-only view/reference to a contiguous sequence of characters

questions.explanation: std::string_view provides zero-copy read-only access to character sequences without allocation.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Can a `constexpr` function in C++14 contain loops and conditional statements?

options.A: Yes, C++14 relaxed constexpr restrictions allowing local variables, loops, and branches
options.B: No, constexpr functions can only contain a single return statement

questions.explanation: C++14 expanded constexpr capabilities to allow local variables, loops, if statements, and mutations.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is placement new in C++?

options.A: Overload of operator new that constructs an object in a pre-allocated memory buffer address: `new (ptr) Type(args)`

questions.explanation: Placement new constructs an object directly into a caller-supplied memory address without allocating heap memory.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What occurs when signed integer overflow happens in standard C++ (`int x = INT_MAX + 1;`)?

options.A: Undefined Behavior
options.B: Wraps around cleanly using two's complement

questions.explanation: Signed integer overflow is strictly Undefined Behavior in standard C++ (unlike unsigned integer overflow which wraps).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the behavior of unsigned integer overflow in C++ (`unsigned int x = UINT_MAX + 1;`)?

options.A: Defined behavior: modulo arithmetic reduction (wraps to 0)

questions.explanation: Unsigned integer arithmetic is defined by C++ standard to obey modular arithmetic (2^N reduction).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is an rvalue reference in C++11 declared with `T&&`?

options.A: A reference that can bind to temporary objects (rvalues), enabling move semantics
options.D: A const reference to lvalues only

questions.explanation: Rvalue references `T&&` bind to temporary objects, allowing resources to be moved rather than copied.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is Variadic Template in C++11?

options.A: A template that can accept a variable number of template arguments using parameter packs `typename... Args`
options.B: A template with variable variable types
options.C: A template for variadic functions only

questions.explanation: Variadic templates accept arbitrary numbers of template parameters using parameter pack syntax `typename... Args`.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the difference between `std::shared_ptr` and `std::unique_ptr` memory footprint?

options.A: std::unique_ptr has zero memory overhead (same size as raw pointer); std::shared_ptr stores extra control block pointer

questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr carries no overhead over a raw pointer, while std::shared_ptr contains two pointers (object pointer + control block pointer).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens if a class defines a move constructor but no copy constructor, and an object is copied?

options.A: Compilation Error (implicitly generated copy operations are deleted when a move operation is declared)

questions.explanation: Declaring a move constructor suppresses the automatic generation of copy constructor/assignment operator.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What does `typeid` operator return in C++ when RTTI is enabled?

options.A: A reference to a const `std::type_info` object representing the object's dynamic type

questions.explanation: typeid returns a const std::type_info& containing type metadata at runtime.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Can a constructor be declared `virtual` in C++?

options.A: No, constructors cannot be virtual in C++

questions.explanation: Constructors cannot be virtual because object dynamic type is established during construction, and vtable pointer is initialized during construction.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Can a destructor be declared `virtual` in C++?

options.A: Yes, virtual destructors ensure proper cleanup in polymorphic inheritance hierarchies

questions.explanation: Virtual destructors are essential in base classes to guarantee derived class destructor execution on dynamic deletion.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: In C++14, what is a Generic Lambda?

options.A: A lambda whose parameter list uses `auto` (`[](auto x, auto y) { return x + y; }`)
options.B: A lambda declared inside template class

questions.explanation: C++14 introduced generic lambdas using `auto` parameters, turning the closure's `operator()` into a template method.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the result of using `std::any` introduced in C++17?

options.A: A type-safe container for single values of any copy-constructible type

questions.explanation: std::any can hold an instance of any copy-constructible type safely.
